title: STK11/LKB1 Mutations and PD-1 Inhibitor Resistance in KRAS-Mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma
design: Retrospective multi-cohort (SU2C + validation) plus murine models
exposure_comparison: PD-1 axis inhibitors; KRAS/STK11 (KL) vs KRAS/TP53 (KP) vs K-only
key_result: ORR to PD-1 blockade 7.4% (KL) vs 35.7% (KP) vs 28.6% (K-only), P<0.001; Stk11 loss promoted PD-(L)1 inhibitor resistance in Kras-mutant mouse models
relevance: Foundational claim that STK11 drives primary ICI resistance; no non-ICI comparator
prognostic_vs_predictive: Claimed predictive (resistance); no control arm so cannot separate from prognostic

title: Diminished Efficacy of Programmed Death-(Ligand)1 Inhibition in STK11- and KEAP1-Mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma Is Affected by KRAS Mutation Status
design: Retrospective multicenter, discovery (DFCI/MGH) + validation (MSKCC/MDACC)
population_n: 1261 advanced LUAD on PD-(L)1 inhibition (620 discovery, 641 validation)
exposure_comparison: PD-(L)1 inhibition; STK11/KEAP1 mutant vs wild-type, stratified by KRAS
key_result: KRAS mutated 42.5%; STK11 mutated 20.6% (260/1261); KEAP1 mutated 19.2% (231/1202). STK11 and KEAP1 mutations conferred worse ICI outcomes in KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wild-type LUAD. HRs ~2.0 in KRAS-mutant seen only in a secondary review table (not confirmed in primary)
relevance: Prevalence for precision planning; motivates KRAS as a second-order modifier (three-way structure)
prognostic_vs_predictive: Prognostic-on-ICI within KRAS strata; no non-ICI or chemo-IO comparator

title: STK11 and KEAP1 mutations as prognostic biomarkers in an observational real-world lung adenocarcinoma cohort
design: Retrospective real-world cohort, Flatiron Health-Foundation Medicine CGDB
population_n: 2276 stage IIIB-IV non-squamous NSCLC; 574 on first-line anti-PD-(L)1
exposure_comparison: Mutation-by-treatment-class interaction (anti-PD-(L)1 vs other first-line therapy)
key_result: No interaction of STK11 mutation with anti-PD-(L)1 treatment: rwPFS HR 1.05 (0.76-1.44), OS HR 1.13 (0.76-1.67). No interaction for KEAP1: rwPFS HR 0.93 (0.67-1.28), OS HR 0.98 (0.66-1.45)
relevance: Closest formal interaction test in real-world data, but the contrast is ICI vs non-ICI, not ICI mono vs chemo-IO
prognostic_vs_predictive: Formally tested; concluded prognostic, not predictive

title: Effects of Co-occurring Genomic Alterations on Outcomes in Patients with KRAS-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
design: Retrospective single-institution (MSK) cohort
exposure_comparison: KEAP1/NFE2L2, STK11, TP53 co-mutation vs none
key_result: KEAP1/NFE2L2 co-mutation: shorter OS (HR 1.96, 95% CI 1.33-2.92, P=0.001), shorter duration of initial chemotherapy and shorter survival from start of immunotherapy; STK11 (HR 1.3, P=0.22) and TP53 (HR 1.11, P=0.58) not associated with OS
relevance: KEAP1 effect seen on both chemo and ICI, supporting prognostic reading

title: KEAP1-driven co-mutations in lung adenocarcinoma unresponsive to immunotherapy despite high tumor mutational burden
design: Retrospective; blood-based cohort from POPLAR/OAK plus tissue-based validation cohort
exposure_comparison: KEAP1 plus PBRM1/SMARCA4/STK11 co-mutation vs single-mutant vs wild-type, on immunotherapy
key_result: Co-mutated tumours had inferior survival vs single-mutant and wild-type; adverse effect maintained in high-TMB LUAD
relevance: Supports analysing co-mutation (STK11+KEAP1) as a separate exposure level
prognostic_vs_predictive: Mainly prognostic-on-ICI; predictive claim not confirmed here

title: STK11/LKB1 and KEAP1 mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: Prognostic rather than predictive?
design: Narrative review / commentary
exposure_comparison: Review of STK11/KEAP1 effect across ICI and non-ICI therapies
key_result: Concludes studies showed a similar effect of STK11/KEAP1 mutations regardless of treatment received, suggesting prognostic rather than predictive value
relevance: Frames the prognostic-vs-predictive controversy the protocol addresses

title: STK11 alterations in the pan-cancer setting: prognostic and therapeutic implications
design: Retrospective pan-cancer cohort
exposure_comparison: STK11 altered vs wild-type across therapies including immunotherapy
key_result: STK11 alterations associated with poor prognosis regardless of therapy; STK11 alone did not clearly predict worse immunotherapy outcome; STK11+KRAS co-alteration had worse outcomes regardless of treatment type
relevance: Note: this is the pan-cancer STK11 paper; authorship is Krishnamurthy/Goodman/Barkauskas/Kurzrock, not Cordeiro de Lima

title: CTLA4 blockade abrogates KEAP1/STK11-related resistance to PD-(L)1 inhibitors
design: Retrospective clinical cohorts + POSEIDON phase III exploratory analysis + Kras-driven mouse models
exposure_comparison: PD-(L)1 inhibitor + chemo vs dual (PD-L1 + CTLA-4) ICB + chemo vs chemo, by STK11/KEAP1 status
key_result: STK11/KEAP1-altered patients did not benefit from durvalumab + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy; adding tremelimumab was associated with longer survival and better responses; KEAP1 loss strongest genomic predictor of dual-ICB efficacy. (Erratum Nature 2025;639:E19.) HRs not seen in sources
relevance: Strongest evidence that genotype modifies benefit of an ICI regimen choice (dual vs single ICB with chemo); different contrast from ours
prognostic_vs_predictive: Predictive claim (for CTLA-4 addition), from exploratory RCT subgroup analysis

title: Associations of tissue tumor mutational burden and mutational status with clinical outcomes in KEYNOTE-042: pembrolizumab versus chemotherapy for advanced PD-L1-positive NSCLC
design: Retrospective exploratory analysis of phase III RCT (WES)
population_n: 793 with evaluable tTMB; STK11 mutant n=33, KEAP1 mutant n=64, KRAS mutant n=69
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs platinum chemotherapy, by STK11/KEAP1/KRAS status
key_result: OS HR pembrolizumab vs chemo: STK11 mutant 0.37 (0.16-0.86) vs wild-type 0.83 (0.65-1.05); KEAP1 mutant 0.75 (0.42-1.35) vs wild-type 0.78 (0.61-0.99); KRAS mutant 0.42 (0.22-0.81) vs wild-type 0.86 (0.63-1.18)
relevance: Randomised evidence that ICI mono retains benefit over chemo in STK11/KEAP1 mutants; one leg of an indirect mono-vs-chemo-IO comparison
prognostic_vs_predictive: Not predictive of loss of benefit (exploratory, small n)

title: Associations of Tissue Tumor Mutational Burden and Mutational Status With Clinical Outcomes With Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy Versus Chemotherapy For Metastatic NSCLC
design: Retrospective exploratory analysis of phase III RCTs KEYNOTE-189 and KEYNOTE-407 (WES)
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab + platinum chemo vs placebo + chemo, by tTMB and STK11/KEAP1/KRAS status
key_result: Treatment outcomes similar regardless of KEAP1, STK11 or KRAS status; authors conclude these mutations are not useful biomarkers for this regimen. Genotype-specific HRs not seen in sources
relevance: Randomised evidence for the chemo-IO leg; second leg of an indirect comparison

title: STK11 (LKB1) mutations in metastatic NSCLC: Prognostic value in the real world
design: Retrospective real-world cohort, Flatiron Clinico-Genomic Database
population_n: 2407 metastatic NSCLC on first- or second-line IO or chemotherapy (per Flatiron summary)
exposure_comparison: STK11 mutant vs wild-type within IO and within chemotherapy
key_result: STK11 mutation had negative prognostic impact with both IO and chemotherapy; first-line IO OS HR 1.4 (0.9-2.3), P=0.1
relevance: Effect present in both treatment classes

title: Baseline Plasma Tumor Mutation Burden Predicts Response to Pembrolizumab-based Therapy in Patients with Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
design: Single-centre prospective cohort (plasma ctDNA)
population_n: 66 metastatic NSCLC on first-line pembrolizumab +/- chemotherapy
exposure_comparison: pTMB >=16 vs <16 mut/Mb; exploratory STK11/KEAP1/PTEN/ERBB2
key_result: pTMB >=16: median OS not reached vs 8.8 months (HR 0.48, 0.22-1.03, P=0.061); STK11, KEAP1, PTEN, ERBB2 exon 20 mutations more common in patients without durable clinical benefit
relevance: Small; pools mono and chemo-IO. May not be the Aggarwal PD-L1/STK11 paper the requester had in mind

title: Clinical efficacy of atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and chemotherapy in KRAS-mutated non-small cell lung cancer with STK11, KEAP1, or TP53 comutations: subgroup results from the phase III IMpower150 trial
design: Exploratory subgroup analysis of phase III RCT (ctDNA NGS)
exposure_comparison: ABCP vs ACP vs BCP, within KRAS-mutant by STK11/KEAP1/TP53 co-mutation
key_result: STK11 and/or KEAP1 mutation associated with worse OS and PFS across arms; in KRAS-mutant with STK11 and/or KEAP1 co-mutation (44.9%) survival longer with ABCP than ACP or BCP; benefit greater in KEAP1/STK11 wild-type
relevance: Prognostic across arms within an RCT; some attenuation of benefit

title: Clinicopathologic and Genomic Factors Impacting Efficacy of First-Line Chemoimmunotherapy in Advanced NSCLC
design: Retrospective multicenter cohort
population_n: 1285 advanced NSCLC (no EGFR/ALK) on first-line chemoimmunotherapy
exposure_comparison: STK11/KEAP1/SMARCA4 mutant vs wild-type on chemo-IO, by KRAS status
key_result: STK11, KEAP1 or SMARCA4 mutation associated with worse ORR, PFS and OS on chemo-IO; in KRAS-wild-type, KEAP1 and SMARCA4 retained the association but STK11 did not (PFS P=0.16, OS P=0.38)
relevance: Chemo-IO arm only: shows genotype effect persists on chemo-IO, i.e. chemo does not obviously rescue
prognostic_vs_predictive: Prognostic on chemo-IO; no mono comparator

title: Gene Copy Deletion of STK11, KEAP1, and SMARCA4: Clinicopathologic Features and Association With the Outcomes of Immunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy in Nonsquamous NSCLC
design: Retrospective two-centre cohort (DFCI, MSK)
exposure_comparison: Gene copy deletion vs none; outcomes on ICI with or without chemotherapy
key_result: STK11 deletion 14.7%, KEAP1 deletion 13.5%, SMARCA4 deletion 13.7%; deletions correlated with reduced PD-L1 expression and poor chemoimmunotherapy efficacy
relevance: Alteration definition: copy deletions add to mutation prevalence; relevant to exposure definition in GENIE panels
prognostic_vs_predictive: Prognostic on ICI +/- chemo; no formal interaction seen in sources

title: STK11 mutations correlate with poor prognosis for advanced NSCLC treated with first-line immunotherapy or chemo-immunotherapy according to KRAS, TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 status
design: Retrospective single-institution cohort with OAK/POPLAR validation
population_n: 145 first-line IO or chemo-IO non-squamous NSCLC (per ESMO 2023 abstract 1477P)
exposure_comparison: STK11 mutant vs wild-type; IO and chemo-IO pooled
key_result: STK11 mutation: shorter OS, multivariable HR 1.97 (P=0.025); OAK/POPLAR multivariable HR 1.66 (P=0.001); authors state the effect appears unrelated to immunotherapy administration
relevance: Pools mono and chemo-IO; no interaction with regimen reported in sources

journal: Annals of Oncology / Immuno-Oncology and Technology (ESMO IO 2023 abstract 68P)
title: Real-world (RW) outcomes in patients (pts) with metastatic (m) NSCLC and STK11, KEAP1 and/or KRAS mutations (mut) receiving PD-(L)1-based treatment
design: Retrospective real-world cohort, US Flatiron database (conference abstract)
population_n: 682 starting first-line anti-PD-(L)1-based treatment Nov 2016-May 2021; 44% had >=1 mutation of interest
exposure_comparison: STK11/KEAP1/KRAS mutant vs wild-type on PD-(L)1-based regimens (regimens emulating KEYNOTE-024, -189, -407, IMpower150)
key_result: Median OS (months): STK11 mutant 8.9 (n=103) vs wild-type 17.6; KEAP1 mutant 9.9 vs 16.3; KRAS mutant 11.6 vs 16.7; no mutation 18.2 (n=382), one mutation 15.3, co-mutation 8.3. Adjusted: STK11 mutation 46% and KRAS mutation 28% increased risk of death; KEAP1 not significant after adjustment
relevance: Best real-world effect sizes for planning; OS by mono vs chemo-IO within genotype not seen in sources

title: MYSTIC exploratory analysis: mutations associated with sensitivity or resistance to immunotherapy in mNSCLC (exact title unverified)
design: Exploratory ctDNA analysis of phase III RCT (GuardantOMNI)
exposure_comparison: Durvalumab vs durvalumab + tremelimumab vs chemotherapy, by STK11/KEAP1/ARID1A status
key_result: STK11 or KEAP1 mutant vs wild-type median OS (months): durvalumab 10.3 vs 13.3; durvalumab + tremelimumab 4.4 vs 11.3; chemotherapy 6.7 vs 13.1 (worse in all arms)
relevance: Randomised evidence that STK11/KEAP1 is adverse in ICI and chemotherapy arms alike

title: Overall survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer with KRAS G12C mutation with or without STK11 and/or KEAP1 mutations in a real-world setting
design: Retrospective real-world clinico-genomic cohort
population_n: 2715 advanced NSCLC without other actionable drivers; 454 (16.7%) KRAS G12C
exposure_comparison: KRAS G12C vs wild-type; STK11/KEAP1 co-mutation; by first-/second-line regimen class
key_result: OS comparable between KRAS G12C and KRAS wild-type on chemotherapy or chemo-IO; first-line immunotherapy alone numerically longer in G12C (30.2 vs 10.6 months); STK11+KEAP1 co-mutation associated with significantly shorter survival independent of KRAS G12C
relevance: Reports outcomes by regimen class and genotype in real-world data; no formal interaction seen in sources

title: Precision Immunotherapy for STK11/KEAP1-Mutant NSCLC
design: Perspective / narrative review
exposure_comparison: Review of ICI strategies in STK11/KEAP1-mutant NSCLC
key_result: States that even with PD-L1 >=50%, STK11 and KEAP1 mutations are associated with worse PFS and OS on PD-(L)1 monotherapy and that combination strategies deserve consideration; ICIs remain a standard first-line option
relevance: Expert framing of the clinical question; acknowledges absence of direct comparative evidence

title: Durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus chemotherapy in first-line metastatic NSCLC: 5-year overall survival from POSEIDON (exact title unverified)
design: Phase III RCT long-term follow-up with exploratory mutation subgroups
exposure_comparison: Tremelimumab + durvalumab + chemo vs chemo; subgroups STK11, KEAP1, KRAS mutant
key_result: OS benefit of the triplet maintained after >5 years and evident in STK11-mutant, KEAP1-mutant and KRAS-mutant subgroups; subgroup HRs 0.57 (STK11), 0.43 (KEAP1), 0.55 (KRAS) reported in ESMO presentation coverage, not confirmed against the paper
relevance: Context for dual-ICB alternative in the mutant subgroup

title: Long-term overall survival with dual CTLA-4 and PD-L1 or PD-1 blockade and biomarker-based subgroup analyses in patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis
design: Systematic review and reconstructed-IPD meta-analysis of 6 phase III RCTs
exposure_comparison: Dual CTLA-4 + PD-(L)1 blockade vs single PD-(L)1 blockade (with or without chemo)
key_result: Overall median OS 16.1 vs 16.9 months (HR 0.95, P=0.19); STK11-mutant median OS 13.9 (dual) vs 7.8 months (single)
relevance: Gives median OS for STK11-mutant on single PD-(L)1-based regimens from trials (7.8 months)
prognostic_vs_predictive: Suggests predictive for CTLA-4 addition (indirect, reconstructed data)

journal: Journal of Clinical Oncology (ASCO 2025 abstract e20504)
title: Impact of mutant STK11, KEAP1, and KRAS on firstline chemoimmunotherapy survival outcomes in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): A meta-analysis of randomized and comparative studies
design: Meta-analysis (6 RCTs + 1 retrospective comparative study); conference abstract
exposure_comparison: Chemo-IO vs chemotherapy within STK11-, KEAP1-, KRAS-mutant subgroups
key_result: Chemo-IO retained OS benefit vs chemotherapy: STK11 mutant HR 0.80 (0.67-0.97), KEAP1 mutant HR 0.76, KRAS mutant HR 0.67
relevance: Chemo-IO vs chemo leg by genotype; not mono vs chemo-IO

journal: Journal of Thoracic Oncology (WCLC 2025 abstract P1.11.69)
title: Efficacy of Immunotherapy +/- Chemotherapy in Metastatic NSCLC with KRAS, STK11, or KEAP1 Mutations: A Network Meta-Analysis
design: Network meta-analysis of trial subgroups (conference abstract)
exposure_comparison: PD-(L)1 mono vs PD-(L)1 + chemo vs PD-(L)1 + CTLA-4 + chemo vs chemo, by genotype (indirect)
key_result: Rankings favoured PD-(L)1 + CTLA-4 + chemo for KEAP1-mutant, PD-(L)1 monotherapy for STK11- and KRAS-mutant, and PD-(L)1 + chemo for wild-type
relevance: Only located work comparing mono vs chemo-IO by STK11/KEAP1 genotype, and only indirectly from trial subgroups
prognostic_vs_predictive: Indirect suggestion of effect modification; abstract only

title: Efficacy of PD-(L)1 blockade monotherapy compared with PD-(L)1 blockade plus chemotherapy in first-line PD-L1-positive advanced lung adenocarcinomas: a cohort study
design: Retrospective two-centre cohort (MSK, DFCI); IPTW Cox models using propensity scores
exposure_comparison: First-line PD-(L)1 monotherapy vs platinum-doublet chemo + PD-(L)1; subgroups by PD-L1, smoking, genomics
key_result: Chemo-IO vs IO in PD-L1 >=1%: ORR 44% vs 35% (P=0.007), PFS HR 0.84 (0.72-0.97, P=0.021); only never-smokers with PD-L1 >=50% had differential survival benefit (P=0.013); no difference at PD-L1 >=90%; abstract states no genomic factors conferred differential survival benefit to chemo-IO vs IO. Which genes and the interaction estimates were not seen
relevance: CLOSEST PRIOR WORK: same contrast with genomic subgroup analysis in academic-centre LUAD; null for genomics. Gene-level STK11/KEAP1 interaction estimates and CIs not verified
prognostic_vs_predictive: Tested differential benefit; null for genomic factors (likely underpowered; details unverified)

title: Effectiveness of PD-(L)1 inhibitors alone or in combination with platinum-doublet chemotherapy in first-line (1L) non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer (Nsq-NSCLC) with PD-L1-high expression using real-world data
design: Retrospective real-world cohort, Flatiron Health EHR-derived database
population_n: 520 metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, PD-L1 >=50% (351 mono, 169 chemo-IO)
exposure_comparison: First-line ICI monotherapy vs ICI + platinum chemotherapy
key_result: Median rwPFS 10.8 (chemo-IO) vs 11.5 months (mono), adjusted HR 1.04; chemo-IO better only in never-smokers (n=50): OS HR 0.25, interaction P=0.02. No genomic subgroup reported in sources
relevance: Same contrast in real-world data; no STK11/KEAP1 analysis. Candidate PMID 35218887 appeared as a search-result URL only
prognostic_vs_predictive: Not applicable (no genotype); smoking tested as modifier

title: Association Between KRAS Variant Status and Outcomes With First-line Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Based Therapy in Patients With Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
design: Retrospective real-world cohort, Flatiron Health (research letter)
exposure_comparison: ICI monotherapy vs chemo-IO, stratified by KRAS status
key_result: ICI mono: median OS 21.1 months (KRAS variant) vs 13.6 months (KRAS wild-type), P=0.03; chemo-IO: 20.0 vs 19.3 months (no difference by KRAS)
relevance: Direct methodological precedent: genotype-by-regimen heterogeneity for the same contrast, but for KRAS not STK11/KEAP1
prognostic_vs_predictive: Suggests KRAS modifies mono-vs-chemo-IO effect (predictive direction)

title: Outcomes of anti-PD-(L)1 therapy with or without chemotherapy for first-line treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer with PD-L1 score >=50%: FDA pooled analysis
design: FDA pooled exploratory analysis of 12 RCTs (cross-trial comparison); no full journal article found
population_n: 3189 pooled; 1753 in OS analysis (26% chemo-IO, 74% IO alone)
exposure_comparison: Chemo-IO vs IO alone, PD-L1 >=50%
key_result: Median OS 25.0 vs 20.9 months (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.62-1.08); median PFS 9.6 vs 7.1 months (HR 0.69); ORR 61% vs 43%. No genomic subgroups
relevance: Main-effect benchmark for the contrast; no peer-reviewed JCO 2024 article could be located

title: Outcomes of first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors with or without chemotherapy according to KRAS mutational status and PD-L1 expression in patients with advanced NSCLC: FDA pooled analysis (exact title unverified)
design: FDA pooled retrospective analysis of 12 registrational trials
population_n: 1430 with KRAS status (61% wild-type, 39% mutated; 555 KRAS-mutant, 157 G12C)
exposure_comparison: ICI alone vs chemo-ICI vs chemo, by KRAS status
key_result: ORR wild-type vs KRAS-mutant: ICI 33% vs 37%, chemo 32% vs 33%, chemo-ICI 51% vs 46%; median OS on chemo-ICI 22.4 (KRAS-mutant) vs 18.7 months (wild-type); authors noted they could not account for STK11/KEAP1 co-mutations
relevance: FDA-level analysis explicitly leaves STK11/KEAP1 unaddressed
prognostic_vs_predictive: Not predictive for KRAS; STK11/KEAP1 not assessed

title: PD-(L)1 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs Chemoimmunotherapy for Advanced NSCLC With High PD-L1 Expression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
design: Systematic review, network meta-analysis and reconstructed-IPD analysis of 24 phase III RCTs
population_n: 5546 (16 chemo-IO trials, 8 mono trials); reconstructed IPD 704 chemo-IO vs 1706 mono
exposure_comparison: Chemo-IO vs PD-(L)1 monotherapy, PD-L1 >=50% (indirect)
key_result: Median OS 29.2 (25.2-35.4) vs 19.8 (18.3-21.7) months, HR 0.74 (0.66-0.82); median PFS 11.3 vs 6.8 months (HR 0.67); meta-regression OS HR 0.85 (borderline). Secondary coverage states STK11/KEAP1 status could not be evaluated
relevance: Most recent main-effect estimate (published online 4 June 2026); explicitly cannot address genotype

title: Pembrolizumab with or without platinum-based chemotherapy as first-line treatment in advanced NSCLC expressing PD-L1 >=50%: The PERSEE randomized phase III trial (GFPC 01-2020)
design: Open-label randomized phase III trial, 28 French centres (NCT04547504)
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab + platinum chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab alone, PD-L1 >=50%
key_result: Met primary endpoint: PFS significantly longer with the combination. Median PFS 16.1 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.56 reported in secondary/social coverage only (not confirmed in the paper); OS described as a numerical trend. No STK11/KEAP1 subgroup results seen
relevance: First randomised head-to-head for the contrast; shifts equipoise toward chemo-IO; genotype subgroup data not located

title: INSIGNA: first-line pembrolizumab alone vs pembrolizumab + pemetrexed/carboplatin strategies in advanced non-squamous NSCLC
design: Randomized phase III trial, ongoing
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab induction/sequencing vs pembrolizumab + pemetrexed-platinum; PD-L1 stratified at 50%
key_result: No results found as of this search (Nov 2026); described as ongoing in the 2026 PERSEE publication
relevance: Randomised answer to the main effect is pending; genomic subgroup plans unverified

title: Deletions on 9p21 are associated with worse outcomes after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy but not chemoimmunotherapy
design: Retrospective real-world clinico-genomic database cohort (database name not confirmed in sources)
population_n: 442 mono-IO and 915 chemo-IO first-line non-squamous NSCLC
exposure_comparison: Genomic alteration vs wild-type, separately within mono-IO and chemo-IO
key_result: CDKN2A deletion: worse survival on mono-IO (HR 1.8, P=0.001) but not chemo-IO (HR 1.1, P=0.4); median OS 15.7 (mono-IO) vs 12.3 months (chemo-IO); among chemo-IO patients STK11, SMARCA4 and KEAP1 alterations associated with worse survival; STK11 alterations more frequent in chemo-IO-treated patients
relevance: Design template: gene effect contrasted across mono-IO vs chemo-IO; also shows confounding by indication (STK11 enriched in chemo-IO via low PD-L1)
prognostic_vs_predictive: Regimen-specific prognostic effects; a formal STK11/KEAP1-by-regimen interaction was not seen in sources

title: Outcomes following first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors with or without chemotherapy stratified by KRAS mutational status: a real-world analysis in patients with advanced NSCLC
design: Retrospective real-world cohort, Tempus database
population_n: 1980 advanced NSCLC on first-line ICI-containing therapy; 662 (33.4%) KRAS-mutant
exposure_comparison: ICI +/- chemotherapy; Cox models stratified by KRAS, PD-L1, and STK11/KEAP1/TP53 alterations
key_result: KRAS G12C with high PD-L1 had the longest median OS (30.28 months, from related abstract); pathogenic KEAP1 and STK11 mutations correlated with worse outcomes in KRAS-mutant tumours
relevance: Real-world ICI +/- chemo cohort with STK11/KEAP1 annotated; a genotype-by-regimen interaction was not seen in sources

title: Real-world comparison of pembrolizumab alone and combined with chemotherapy in metastatic lung adenocarcinoma patients with PD-L1 expression >=50%
design: Retrospective nationwide registry cohort (Norway)
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs pembrolizumab + chemotherapy
key_result: Combination gave superior early survival benefit over monotherapy in PD-L1-high patients; reported greater benefit in females, stage IVB and PD-L1 >75%. HRs not seen; no STK11/KEAP1 analysis seen
relevance: Real-world mono vs chemo-IO; non-proportional (early) effect supports RMST

title: Pembrolizumab versus Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer with High PD-L1 Expression - Multicenter Real-world Evidence Study
design: Retrospective multicentre Central European cohort with matching
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs pembrolizumab + chemotherapy, PD-L1 >=50%
key_result: Unadjusted median OS 26.8 (combination) vs 18.5 months (monotherapy); no differences in survival after matching. No STK11/KEAP1 breakdown
relevance: Illustrates that crude differences vanish after confounding adjustment

title: Real-World Immunotherapy Use and Effectiveness in Advanced NSCLC With Programmed Death-Ligand 1 Greater Than or Equal to 50% and Greater Than or Equal to 90%
design: Retrospective real-world cohort (Ottawa)
exposure_comparison: Pembrolizumab-based first-line therapy by PD-L1 level (>=50% vs >=90%)
key_result: Most PD-L1-high patients received pembrolizumab monotherapy; OS tracked PD-L1 level, substantially longer at PD-L1 >=90%
relevance: PD-L1 level within >=50% is a strong confounder/modifier; GENIE BPC PD-L1 completeness matters

title: The GENIE BPC NSCLC Cohort: A Real-World Repository Integrating Standardized Clinical and Genomic Data for 1,846 Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
design: Cohort description; multi-institution clinicogenomic registry curated with PRISSMM
exposure_comparison: Descriptive; treatment-specific outcomes; KRAS +/- STK11/KEAP1 on first-line platinum
key_result: Median OS on first-line platinum without immunotherapy 17.4 months (14.9-19.5); KRAS subgroups on first-line platinum: KRAS alone n=113, KRAS+STK11 n=31, KRAS+KEAP1 n=4 (shows very small genotype-by-regimen cells)
relevance: Planned data source; signals that precision for STK11/KEAP1-by-regimen cells will be limited

title: Correlation Between Surrogate End Points and Overall Survival in a Multiinstitutional Clinicogenomic Cohort of Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung or Colorectal Cancer
design: Retrospective cohort, GENIE BPC (four academic centres), PRISSMM-curated endpoints
exposure_comparison: Real-world PFS definitions, time to treatment discontinuation, time to next treatment vs OS
key_result: PFS based on imaging plus medical oncologist documentation correlated most strongly with OS (NSCLC rho=0.76; CRC rho=0.73); time to treatment discontinuation correlated least
relevance: Justifies choice of PRISSMM PFS-I-and-M as secondary endpoint

title: A data processing pipeline for the AACR project GENIE biopharma collaborative data with the {genieBPC} R package
design: Software / methods paper
exposure_comparison: Not applicable
key_result: Describes the genieBPC R package for pulling BPC releases from Synapse and building analytic cohorts for clinico-genomic analyses
relevance: Cohort construction tool for the protocol

title: Implications of Selection Bias Due to Delayed Study Entry in Clinical Genomic Studies
design: Methods study using GENIE BPC data
exposure_comparison: Naive vs left-truncation (risk-set) adjusted survival estimation
key_result: Ignoring delayed entry overestimated median OS from diagnosis in stage IV NSCLC or CRC by more than a year; risk-set adjustment available in standard software
relevance: Mandates left-truncation handling when index date precedes sequencing

title: Impact of KRAS, STK11 and KEAP1 co-mutations on survival outcome and response to chemoimmunotherapy in patients with metastatic NSCLC
design: Retrospective analysis of AACR GENIE data (conference abstract; whether BPC specifically is unverified)
population_n: 1004 metastatic NSCLC with KRAS/STK11/KEAP1 status; triple-mutant 4.7%
exposure_comparison: Chemo-IO vs chemotherapy within KRAS/STK11/KEAP1 groups
